title: Are All Odd Zeta Values Transcendental?
description: Formalizes the open question: are all odd zeta values ζ(2k+1) transcendental? Proves even zeta transcendence (ζ(2), ζ(4)) from Lindemann axiom, axiomatizes Apéry's theorem (ζ(3) irrational), and establishes structural implications: transcendence conjecture ⟹ irrationality conjecture ⟹ known results.

overview.historicalContext: The even zeta values ζ(2k) = rational × π^(2k) have been fully understood since Euler (1734) and Lindemann (1882): they are all transcendental. The odd zeta values ζ(2k+1) remain deeply mysterious. Not a single one has been proved transcendental. Even the weaker question of irrationality is largely open: Apéry (1978) proved ζ(3) irrational in a tour de force, Rivoal (2000) showed infinitely many odd ζ are irrational, and Zudilin (2001) pinpointed ζ(5,7,9,11) as containing at least one irrational. But beyond these partial results, specific odd zeta values remain out of reach.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Conjecture**: For all k ≥ 1, ζ(2k+1) is transcendental over ℚ.

Not a single odd zeta value is known to be transcendental. Even ζ(3) — the only specific odd zeta value known to be irrational — has unknown transcendence status.

**Known hierarchy**:
- Transcendence conjecture ⟹ Irrationality conjecture
- Irrationality conjecture ⟹ Apéry theorem
- Irrationality conjecture ⟹ Rivoal theorem
- Irrationality conjecture ⟹ Zudilin theorem
overview.text: A 274-line formalization of the arithmetic landscape of odd zeta values. Defines zetaValue(s) = ∑ 1/n^s and proves the closed forms ζ(2) = π²/6 and ζ(4) = π⁴/90 from Mathlib. Two deep results are axiomatized: Lindemann's theorem (π transcendental) and Apéry's theorem (ζ(3) irrational). Proves even-zeta transcendence (ζ(2) and ζ(4)) from the Lindemann axiom. States the transcendence and irrationality conjectures, then proves structural implications connecting them.
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization proceeds in layers:

**Layer 1 (Mathlib)**: Closed forms ζ(2) = π²/6, ζ(4) = π⁴/90 from hasSum_zeta_two/four.

**Layer 2 (Axioms)**: Two deep results not in Mathlib — Lindemann (π transcendental), Apéry (ζ(3) irrational).

**Layer 3 (Proved)**: Even-zeta transcendence: ζ(2) and ζ(4) proved transcendental from Lindemann axiom via transcendental_pow_of_transcendental.

**Layer 4 (Conjectures)**: The transcendence and irrationality conjectures for odd zeta values as Prop definitions.

**Layer 5 (Structure)**: Proved implications: transcendence ⟹ irrationality (via Transcendental.irrational), conjecture specializes to Apéry (k=1).
keyInsights: The even/odd divide in zeta values is one of the starkest in number theory: complete understanding vs near-total mystery
Rivoal's theorem is best formalized using Set.Infinite rather than quantified Finset bounds — cleaner and more compositional
The full implication chain (transcendence → irrationality → all known results) is provable without sorry
Even-zeta transcendence needs: if π is transcendental, then π^n/q is transcendental for n ≥ 1, q ∈ ℚ×. This requires Mathlib's algebraic closure infrastructure.

Zudilin's 4-way disjunction (one of ζ(5,7,9,11) irrational) is the tightest known finite explicit bound — improving it to a 3-way or 2-way disjunction remains open and would require fundamentally new ideas in Padé approximation

sections.title: Zeta Values at Natural Numbers
sections.summary: Definition of zetaValue(s) = ∑ 1/n^s as a tsum over ℕ.
sections.mathContext: $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}$ for $s > 1$. Defined via `tsum` (topological sum) in Lean, converging absolutely for $s \geq 2$. Euler computed $\zeta(2k) = (-1)^{k+1} B_{2k} (2\pi)^{2k} / (2(2k)!)$ where $B_{2k}$ are Bernoulli numbers.

sections.title: Known Even Zeta Values
sections.summary: ζ(2) = π²/6 and ζ(4) = π⁴/90 proved directly from Mathlib.
sections.mathContext: $\zeta(2) = \pi^2/6$ (Basel problem, Euler 1734) and $\zeta(4) = \pi^4/90$. Both are instances of Euler's general formula $\zeta(2k) = (-1)^{k+1} B_{2k} (2\pi)^{2k}/(2(2k)!)$. The closed forms involve $\pi^{2k}$, making even zeta values transcendental — in stark contrast to odd zeta values where no closed form is known.

sections.title: Deep Axioms
sections.summary: Lindemann's theorem (π transcendental) and Apéry's theorem (ζ(3) irrational) axiomatized.
sections.mathContext: Two deep axioms: (1) $\pi \notin \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ (Lindemann 1882) and (2) $\zeta(3) \notin \mathbb{Q}$ (Apéry 1978). Lindemann proved $e^\alpha$ is transcendental for nonzero algebraic $\alpha$; since $e^{i\pi} = -1$, this forces $\pi$ transcendental. Apéry's proof used rapidly convergent series for $\zeta(3)$ with carefully constructed rational approximations.

sections.title: The Open Conjectures
sections.summary: Transcendence and irrationality conjectures for odd zeta values.
sections.mathContext: Two conjectures: (1) $\zeta(2k+1) \notin \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ for all $k \geq 1$ (transcendence), (2) $\zeta(2k+1) \notin \mathbb{Q}$ for all $k \geq 1$ (irrationality). The transcendence conjecture implies the irrationality conjecture. Neither has been proved for any single value beyond $\zeta(3)$.

sections.title: Even vs Odd Zeta Values
sections.summary: Definition of the rational multiple property for even zeta values.
sections.mathContext: Even zeta values satisfy $\zeta(2k) = r_k \cdot \pi^{2k}$ with $r_k \in \mathbb{Q}^\times$ (e.g., $r_1 = 1/6$, $r_2 = 1/90$). Odd zeta values have NO known analogous representation — this even/odd dichotomy is one of the deepest mysteries in analytic number theory.

sections.title: Even Zeta Transcendence
sections.summary: ζ(2) and ζ(4) transcendence theorems, fully proved from Lindemann axiom via transcendental_pow_of_transcendental.

sections.title: Deep Results on Odd Zeta Irrationality
sections.summary: Even-odd hierarchy theorem connecting ζ(2) transcendence, ζ(3) irrationality (Apéry), and structural relationships.
sections.mathContext: Rivoal (2000): infinitely many $\zeta(2k+1)$ are irrational. Zudilin (2001): at least one of $\zeta(5), \zeta(7), \zeta(9), \zeta(11)$ is irrational. Both are axiomatized. The hierarchy: $\zeta(2)$ transcendental (proved) $\supset$ $\zeta(3)$ irrational (Apéry, axiom) $\supset$ $\zeta(5)$ irrationality (open).

sections.title: The Irrationality Landscape
sections.summary: Proved: irrationality conjecture implies Rivoal and Zudilin; transcendence conjecture recovers all known results.
sections.mathContext: The implication landscape: $\forall k,\, \zeta(2k+1) \notin \mathbb{Q}$ implies Rivoal's 'infinitely many irrational' and Zudilin's 'one of $\{\zeta(5),\zeta(7),\zeta(9),\zeta(11)\}$ irrational'. The stronger transcendence conjecture $\forall k,\, \zeta(2k+1) \notin \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ recovers ALL known results as corollaries — a strong consistency check.

sections.title: Odd Zeta Transcendence and Irrationality Conjectures

Defines the weaker $	ext{odd\_zeta\_irrationality\_conjecture}$: all odd zeta values are irrational. Notes that no specific odd zeta value beyond $\zeta(3)$ has been proved irrational.

sections.title: Structural Relationships Between Conjectures
sections.summary: Proves the logical chain: transcendence conjecture implies irrationality conjecture, which implies Apery's theorem ($\zeta(3)$ irrational) as the $k=1$ case, and further implies joint irrationality of $\zeta(3)$ and $\zeta(5)$.

sections.title: The Even-Odd Divide and Problem Status
sections.summary: Defines $	ext{even\_zeta\_rational\_multiple}$: $\zeta(2k) = q \cdot \pi^{2k}$ for rational $q$. Verifies transcendence of $\zeta(2)$ and $\zeta(4)$ from axiomatized Lindemann. Proves the arithmetic hierarchy: $\zeta(2)$ transcendental, $\zeta(3)$ irrational (Apery), $\zeta(5)$ status unknown.
sections.mathContext: Even-odd dichotomy: $\zeta(2k) = c_k \pi^{2k}$ (transcendental via Lindemann) vs. $\zeta(2k+1)$ with no known closed form. Arithmetic hierarchy: transcendental \supset irrational \supset algebraic.

conclusion.summary: This formalization maps the frontier of odd zeta value arithmetic. Two deep axioms (Lindemann, Apéry) anchor the formalization, with even-zeta transcendence (ζ(2), ζ(4)) fully proved from the Lindemann axiom. Structural implications connect the transcendence and irrationality conjectures to known results. 0 sorries remain.
conclusion.implications:
**If the transcendence conjecture were proved**: All known partial results follow as corollaries. More importantly, the techniques would likely revolutionize analytic number theory — current methods (hypergeometric series, Padé approximants) cannot even prove irrationality of ζ(5) individually.

**For formalization**: The even-zeta transcendence proofs await Mathlib's algebraic number theory infrastructure — specifically, that rational multiples of transcendental powers remain transcendental. Once Lindemann-Weierstrass enters Mathlib, pi_transcendental can be upgraded from axiom to theorem.
openQuestions: Is ζ(3) transcendental? (The most accessible individual case)
Is any specific odd zeta value transcendental?
Are ζ(3), ζ(5), ζ(7), ... algebraically independent over ℚ?
Can the Ball-Rivoal method be refined to prove individual irrationality results?

mainTheorems.name: zetaValue_two_transcendental
mainTheorems.description: ζ(2) = π²/6 is transcendental, proved from the Lindemann axiom (π transcendental) via transcendental_pow_of_transcendental — the first machine-verified even-zeta transcendence result.

mainTheorems.name: transcendental_pow_of_transcendental
mainTheorems.description: If x is transcendental then x^n is transcendental for n ≥ 1, providing the algebraic backbone for deriving ζ(2) and ζ(4) transcendence from π transcendence.

mainTheorems.name: even_odd_hierarchy
mainTheorems.description: Structural implication chain connecting ζ(2) transcendence with the irrationality conjecture for odd zeta values, showing the transcendence conjecture implies all known partial results as corollaries.

references.title: Über die Zahl π
references.note: Proved π is transcendental ($e^\alpha$ transcendental for nonzero algebraic $\alpha$), establishing the key axiom used here for even-zeta transcendence

references.title: Irrationalité de ζ(2) et ζ(3)
references.note: Proved the irrationality of $\zeta(3)$ using rapidly convergent series and clever recurrences — the only odd zeta value whose irrationality is known individually. The proof stunned the mathematical community and remains the gold standard for Diophantine approximation to zeta values

references.title: La fonction zêta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs
references.venue: Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, vol. 331(4), pp. 267-270
references.note: Proved that infinitely many odd zeta values $\zeta(2k+1)$ are irrational — a breakthrough that went beyond Apéry's single result for $\zeta(3)$

references.title: One of the numbers ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational
references.note: Sharpened Rivoal's result to a finite explicit disjunction: at least one of four specific odd zeta values is irrational. The tightest known explicit bound on which odd zeta values are irrational

references.authors: Fischler, Stéphane; Sprang, Johannes; Zudilin, Wadim
references.title: Many odd zeta values are irrational
references.note: Proved that among $\zeta(3), \zeta(5), \ldots, \zeta(s)$, at least $(1-\varepsilon)\frac{\log s}{1+\log 2}$ are irrational — the current state of the art, dramatically extending Rivoal's qualitative result
